answers.reason: The representative is elected only at the faculty level and does not hold a university-wide office.
Central budget planning is reserved for university leadership and central administration, not faculty student representatives.
As the elected representative of the faculty's students, this person fills the statutory student seat on faculty appointment committees.
The elected student representative holds an office specifically created to represent students in the faculty's main governing council.
Student representatives are formally included in faculty commissions dealing with teaching and degree programmes.
Formal examination boards at the faculty level typically include a seat for an elected student representative.
Awarding internal research grants is a research matter where student representatives do not hold a statutory seat.
Because the representative holds a faculty-level office in teaching matters, they may participate in subordinate working groups on study programmes.
Equipment procurement is an administrative and faculty staff matter without a designated seat for student representatives.
Planning the orientation week for new students directly concerns student affairs, permitting the elected student representative to take part.
